repairs.rationale: Authentication traffic and stored identity data require the platform-wide encryption contract.

The R2 Stripe boundary consumes the proven Convex schema assembler, Customer genesis contract, current price authority, retention classification, role and API/UI authorization, informational seat and pooled-wallet projections, accessibility proof, canary process, and private rollout controls before subscription, invoice, metering, rollback, and customer proof can close. F-631's closed customer-flag catalog is not a private Stripe-control owner.
The Organization contract requires the typed Convex Preview foundation and the per-service test gate before its schema, isolation, recovery, and migration proof can execute.

Buyer Workspace reads and lists are console-scoped and must enforce org_id plus console query scoping, the deny-by-default cross-origin registry, and the application-header policy before the R0 shell is exposed.

MarketplaceReview and MarketplaceIntegrationHook require the database foundation, canonical AuditEvent writer, Marketplace Listing base entity, and Marketplace discovery authority before their cross-console source, moderation, handoff, recovery, and proof paths can execute.

The immutable PricingTableVersion fragment requires the canonical Convex schema assembler plus the capability and cost-base inputs used by its deterministic snapshot builder. Customer/Ops authorization and lifecycle orchestration remain with the consuming F-499/F-549 owners.

Org Owner authority is an additive Organization-role policy contribution and must consume the canonical role-assignment and membership lifecycle plus the shared API/UI enforcement adapter; it cannot become a competing authorization entrypoint.
The common API/UI authorization adapter consumes the canonical role-feature decision matrix and immutable AuditEvent writer; it must not redefine either source of authority.
Pipeline advancement requires an authorized Workspace owner or member, enforced access, and the common failure-reason-recovery contract.
Phase 1 begins the mandatory journey only with phase locking plus the canonical advancement API, idempotency, audit, and gate validation controls.
Phase 2 follows completion of Phase 1 in the canonical evaluation journey.
Phase 3 follows completion of Phase 2 in the canonical evaluation journey.
Vendor discovery and outreach follow Phase 3 validation and advance Target Accounts through their canonical solicitation lifecycle.
Opening bidding follows vendor discovery and outreach and requires versioned Requirement materialization, bridge redaction, and canonical Requirement and Response transitions.
Phase 7 response refinement follows the opening of vendor bidding in Phase 6.
Phase 8 due diligence follows the Phase 7 response refinement window.
Phase 9 final clarifications follow completion of Phase 8 due diligence and demos.
Phase 10 follows final vendor clarifications and uses the canonical scoring engine and draft-to-locked lifecycle.
Phase 11 score review and consensus follow Phase 10 team evaluation and scoring.
Selection begins only after Phase 11 consensus and its Summary Scoring Report are complete and Phase 12 entry locks the evaluation scores.
Phase 13 closure follows selection and Selection Report generation and performs the canonical Workspace and Bid Workspace state transitions.
Creating the immutable closure bundle requires canonical append-only mutation audit logging, binding retention, and nightly integrity verification.
The R0 Bid Workspace shell must inherit the same deny-by-default cross-origin registry and application-header enforcement as the Buyer Workspace before seller entry is exposed.

Webhook delivery and replay can execute only after the compiled event registry and subscription-registration firewall resolve the current event, console, audience, entitlement, schema, and target contracts.

CRM review activity consumes the canonical MarketplaceReview source and only dispatches through the proved webhook/integration delivery foundation; review publication remains independent of CRM availability.
Replay-safe seat snapshots consume the single canonical BillingSeatSnapshot entity and index contract before scheduled or event-driven computation can write or project informational counts.

The later Buyer-trial notices and terminal conversion or downgrade require the R0 activation row, Stripe subscription completion, the canonical notification catalog, in-app and email delivery, user preferences and inheritance, the Buyer Free target, canonical plan-change behavior, excess-data preservation, and the service test/evidence control plane; activation cannot wait for the later lifecycle release.

Organization-pooled wallet recomputation requires current approved pricing inputs, the canonical AIWallet mutation boundary, and F-630's registered private server-side rollout and kill-switch control before customer-visible mutation; F-631's customer flag catalog is not reused.
Seller setup recovery requires the Settings route and authoritative onboarding state, and the invited-seller checklist must remain suppressed until the first response submission completes.
The canonical retention registry must compile against the authoritative persisted schema and entity inventory; unknown or uncovered storage fails closed before any consumer can delete or move data.

The Enterprise SLA family requires residency-partitioned deployment, the canonical Support Widget intake channel, signed subscription-aware webhook delivery, Buyer/Seller/combined Enterprise plan owners, and monitoring foundations before its canonical contract, monthly uptime measurement, and breach-notification proof can complete.
The per-service test pyramid requires a real, commit-bound Convex Preview deployment for its mandatory integration lane; database mocks are forbidden outside unit tests.

The release gate requires the canonical Convex schema assembler, stable analytics cohort assignment, accessibility proof, monitoring, recovery drills, observability, performance budgets, and the test pyramid before canary and rollback decisions.
Feature-flag decisions must consume the canonical PostHog integration and current entitlement evaluator so the server can enforce entitlement first, flag second, without copying plan rules.

The Network Effects Dashboard consumes the canonical network-effect and S1–S7 signal inventories and renders only inside the §50 Ops Console under its capability-envelope role matrix; the retired F-608 Admin Dashboard is not an executable prerequisite.
The seven-stage onboarding contract requires release-blocking QA plus canonical event families, envelopes, durable delivery, and product analytics properties.

The shared FormField family must consume the canonical form tokens, validation state machine, accessibility foundation, and complete UX token set before its eleven variants can be implemented without per-console drift.
Domain Bootstrap creates KB Entries that must follow the canonical KB Entry lifecycle and indexing transitions.

The end-to-end Pricing Admin publish surface composes the Ops security boundary, proposal, simulation, communications, rate-card, cost-base, free-allowance, public-cache, audit, telemetry, webhook, monitoring, and recovery contracts; none can be deferred without violating §50.12 acceptance criteria.

The Seller Dashboard is a read-only composition over canonical bid, action, KB-health, marketplace, audit, shared-state, and navigation owners; every named section and route must exist before the complete UX §4.3.1 outcome can close.
Application headers require the reproducible three-shell foundation, console isolation, the validated Convex origin pair, and the deny-by-default cross-origin registry before enforcement.
The cross-origin registry requires the reproducible route inventory and dual-console boundary before its empty R0 allowlist and failure contract can be enforced.

Enterprise branding consumes authenticated Organization settings, canonical tokens and contrast rules, audit/Ops controls, the test pyramid, and the all-plan base-logo owner without granting a Seller entitlement.
Reference-data orchestration can run only after template and pricing owners, Ops session/role/state controls, the complete Pricing Admin gate, and commit-bound test evidence exist.

R0 Buyer Org creation must resolve WorkOS identity, User and founding membership; atomically materialize the Organization, active Stripe Customer, TrialState, Business Starter plan, wallet, allowances, and qualified audit; then commit the exact signup-stage UsageEvent/outbox pair under the PostHog taxonomy and standard envelope before exposing a successful Buyer route. F-916 owns only the §48 signup-stage slice; F-636/F-637 retain the later full-funnel stages and their F-527 dependency.

The first Stripe Customer can be bound only after the Organization primitive, canonical Organization-created audit emitter, platform encryption and secret-handling contract, and service test/evidence control plane are available.

The canonical discretionary-Ops audit record requires the current AuditEvent and OpsSession entities, common authorization enforcement, retention registry, monitoring, separated Ops shell/auth/mutation/DB-denial/role controls, and exact analytics envelope before its schema, atomic writer, read firewall, and proof can close.

The full plan-tier override surface composes canonical billing and Organization state, audit/session/authorization, notification/webhook/API/error/monitoring/Ops controls, Pricing Admin authority, accessibility, exact event envelopes, and OpsActionRecord atomicity before two-person publish, effective-date execution, reversal, and recovery can close.

The full Workspace export surface requires canonical console isolation, Organization/Workspace identity, audit/session/authorization, DSAR cascade, secret handling, data export/retention, API/webhook/error/monitoring/Ops controls, accessibility, exact envelopes, and OpsActionRecord atomicity before generation or download can run.

Refund authorization composes Stripe, AuditEvent, OpsSession, AIWallet, ContestRecord, common enforcement, notification/webhook/API/error/retention/monitoring/Ops/accessibility/event controls, and OpsActionRecord; the compressed source contract must be repaired before executable children can earn readiness.

Wallet adjustment composes Stripe, AuditEvent, OpsSession, AIWallet, AIOperation, common enforcement, notification/webhook/API/error/retention/monitoring/Ops/accessibility/event controls, and OpsActionRecord; the compressed source contract must be repaired before executable children can earn readiness.

Trial management composes billing, Organization/trial activation, AuditEvent, OpsSession, common enforcement, notification/webhook/API/error/retention/monitoring/Ops/accessibility/event controls, OpsActionRecord, and PlanTierOverride reuse; the compressed source contract must be repaired before executable children can earn readiness.

Listing moderation composes Marketplace, abuse, listing, webhook/API/error/retention/monitoring/Ops/accessibility/event controls, role enforcement, fraud review, and OpsActionRecord; the compressed source contract must be repaired before executable children can earn readiness.

AIOperation reversal composes Stripe, AuditEvent, OpsSession, AIOperation, AIWallet, ContestRecord, Outcome Resolver, common enforcement, notification/webhook/API/error/retention/monitoring/Ops/accessibility/event controls, and OpsActionRecord; the compressed source contract must be repaired before executable children can earn readiness.

User-account Ops actions compose customer and Ops identity, Organization scope, AuditEvent/OpsSession, service roles, common enforcement, WorkOS/SSO/API-token/SCIM/deprovisioning, notification/webhook/API/error/retention/monitoring/Ops/accessibility/event controls, and OpsActionRecord; the compressed source contract must be repaired before executable children can earn readiness.
